Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first establish the workspace contract from `README.md`, then use the fish-control shelf and the visual-evidence skill before touching the candidate. After that I’ll inspect the inherited rollout evidence, implement exactly one policy in `solver/`, and update both required reasoning files.

I’m using `fish-control-primitives` because the prompt requires the structured transfer consultation, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because this workspace’s policy changes are gated on inspecting both moving-window visual views. I’m reading those instructions in full now; any shelf-derived mechanism will be recorded with the required falsification block.

The assigned evidence is unusually strong in one narrow sense: all four sampled solver examples are threshold captures, so there is no failed sampled solver to compare directly. I’ll inspect all four quantitative records and both visual rows, then use the inherited parent logs to select the nearest genuinely informative failure for the required success/failure contrast.

The visual gate is now satisfied. The strongest sampled capture and the inherited repeat failure both self-propel with a coherent alternating top-down street and bilateral 3D structures; the failure simply passes outside the capture disk and continues an active lower-exit turn. That isolates terminal path geometry from propulsion or wake collapse. I’m now consulting the mechanism shelf against that diagnosis; this is a re-consultation, and I’ll adopt only an invariant that creates a genuinely different feedback mechanism.

The shelf and rollout history point to one small mechanism-level test: restore the evidence-backed carrier and replace the failed additive LOS residual with the previously successful, response-conditioned partial steering-retention gate. This is not a gain sweep—the intervention changes when an incompatible projected pass is allowed to release steering, while leaving the route error and propulsive wave untouched. I’m checking its source-family boundaries and its one existing CFD result before committing to an exact-policy repeat.

The selected exact-repeat candidate is now evidence-bounded: the partial compatibility gate has one direct-uniform capture at `0.74852L`/`18.2985T`, preserves both wake views, and stays inside the baseline actuator/load envelope. The additive LOS controller, by contrast, now has an exact-repeat `1.59620L` lower-exit failure with the carrier still active. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification criteria before replacing the solver candidate, as required.

The solver candidate is now byte-identical to the previously evaluated partial-gate policy (`1059127…`), so this rollout is a clean reliability repeat rather than an untracked variant. I’m now revising the durable experience bank to incorporate the assigned parent’s LOS-repeat failure and the contrasting partial-gate capture; this is the main lesson the shelf consultation changed.

The required candidate, notes, and durable lesson are all in place. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated non-CFD check runner now; it will verify the semantic guidance delta, Julia policy contract where available, and the one-file solver boundary.

Two required checks already pass locally: the guidance update is semantically material (including the parameter-schema guard), and the solver boundary confirms only `candidate_target_policy.jl` changed under `solver/`. The remaining contract probe depends on the check runner’s Julia environment; the workspace shell itself has no `julia` executable on `PATH`.

The mandated runner confirms the two workspace checks pass; only the Julia probe failed before loading the policy because no Julia executable is installed. I’m checking the local module/install paths once so this is an environment limitation rather than a missed runtime location. If no runtime exists, I’ll validate the exact evaluated-byte identity and schema evidence and record the probe limitation explicitly.

A Julia 1.12.6 runtime exists outside `PATH` at `julia`. I’ve supplied that location back to the required check runner so it can rerun the identical non-CFD contract probe and close the only failed check.

All three mandated checks now pass, including the finite two-joint Julia contract probe. I’m recording the exact-byte identity and validation results in the candidate notes, then doing one final read-only audit of the three deliverables.

Implemented exactly one candidate: `dogfish3d_partial_outer_intercept_guard_v1`.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8) — exact repeat of the previously captured partial steering-retention policy.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) — visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, hypothesis, falsification, and validation.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:228) — materially revised lesson rejecting fixed additive LOS-rate interception after its repeat failure.

All required checks pass: semantic guidance/schema, Julia finite-action contract, and solver editable-boundary. Candidate SHA-256 is `1059127f77ddbeac9f8a832d1f922d0d0820a08707327c8fa1799c7ab7467d3f`. No CFD was run.
